correctness.rationale: The weights are positive Banach function weights: their excess over 1 has finite integral. An explicit measure-preserving involution exchanges targets. The maximum-function ratio follows from the displayed geometric and p-series inequalities. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz gives A_i(a)^2=sup_{|E|<=a} integral_E v_i^2/w. Aligned quotient equals n^2 on intervals I_n and 1 elsewhere: exact two-sided bounds ((N-1)^2)a<=A_0(a)^2<=((N-1)^2+3N)a yield the asymptotic constant 1/(4 log 2). Separated quotient has integral 1 on each J_n and arbitrarily many such J_n fit inside any positive measure budget, forcing A_1(a)=infinity. All quantifiers and endpoints apply for all a>0 or a down to 0 as stated; no experiment replaces proof.

value.rationale: The recently introduced minimal/maximal fundamental functions are designed to provide non-rearrangement-invariant tests for small-support norm decay. A positive necessary ratio can appear promising as a criterion; this explicit pair proves that even complete marginal extrema fail to decide it. The obstruction survives genuine Banach-function-space axioms and is isolated to the alignment of weights. The matched positive configuration has a sharp leading logarithmic modulus, while rearranging the same target mass makes every local embedding constant infinite. This is a structural boundary and a quantitative counterexample, not an arbitrary integral recomputation; no universal classification or downstream theorem is claimed.
